samples.question: The dark board is scattered with small decorative coloured squares, and exactly one cream CARD sits somewhere on it. Only what is drawn on the card decides the answer; every square off the card is decoration and means nothing. The card carries three RINGS, each of six small square beads evenly spaced around a circle. Every bead is red, blue, green or purple, and a colour may repeat inside a ring. The single ring at the top of the card is the KEY ring. Below it are two DIAL rings, one on the left and one on the right, and under each dial ring lies one wide coloured BAR. Reading a ring means walking its six beads clockwise, starting at any bead, which gives that ring a closed cyclic colour order. Each dial ring carries exactly the same six bead colours as the key ring. One of the two dials is the key ring turned by some angle, so reading it clockwise gives the key's cyclic order starting somewhere else; the other dial is the key ring flipped over, so reading it clockwise gives the key's cyclic order backwards. Flipping keeps every colour count and keeps every pair of neighbouring beads, so counting colours or checking which colours touch cannot tell the two dials apart - only the clockwise direction of the order can. The two bars have two different colours drawn from red, blue, green and purple, and the bar colours are chosen independently of the beads, so no bead tells you a bar colour. What colour is the bar under the dial ring that is the key ring turned rather than flipped? Answer red, blue, green or purple.
